trust_decision.summary: Genuine missing escape, but narrow: the jsonb_path_exists branch formats the expected literal straight into the JSONPath equality at FilterToSqlHelper.java:803 while the sibling @> branch already escapes at :752; the published fix escapes the same way in one line, at one site.

landing_point.why: An engineer told 'SQL injection in jsonArrayContains against PostGIS' searches the postgis module for the function and lands on encodeJsonArrayContains -> constructEquality, where the string literal is formatted unescaped into the JSONPath equality (and the two sibling call sites at :752 and :768 already call escapeJsonLiteral).

fix_sites.entry_point: PostGISDataStore query encoding (filter supplied by the caller, e.g. an OGC filter) -> PostgisFilterToSQL.visit(Function) (PostgisFilterToSQL.java:126) or PostgisPSFilterToSql.visit(Function) (PostgisPSFilterToSql.java:103), both delegating to FilterToSqlHelper.visitFunction (FilterToSqlHelper.java:680) -> encodeJsonArrayContains (:763) -> constructEquality (:791); prepared vs non-prepared statements is only a configuration of the same entry point

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists. The nearest thing a solver could try to dismiss is the sibling pre-12 '@>' branch as 'a second unprotected route', but it already escapes the value at FilterToSqlHelper.java:752, so dismissing it happens to be correct.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Numeric expectations must stay unquoted bare JSONPath numbers ('@.operations == 1'); a fix that routed every value through string escaping/quoting would break legitimate numeric matching (and the existing test PostgisJsonPathExistsTest.java:66-73). The pre-12 '@>' output must also stay byte-identical (PostgisFilterToSQLTest.java:371-378).

O6_input_shapes: string containing a single quote ("can't" -> can''t)
string containing double quote and single quote ("\"'FOO" -> \"''FOO)
multi-segment pointer (/operations/parameters), where the escaped pointer is split and reused as the JSON key
numeric literal (Integer/Float/Double branch, emitted bare, unquoted)
jsonArrayContains compared to a boolean via ff.equals(...) reaching the same sink through PostgisFilterToSQL.visit(PropertyIsEqualTo) (PostgisFilterToSQL.java:229)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second JSONPath predicate builder for another operator (e.g. like_regex / starts_with) using the same "%s" formatting
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: constructEquality is already the per-operator literal builder; adding another supported JSONPath operator naturally means adding another formatted literal right beside it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a duplicated value-into-JSON builder in the pre-Postgres-12 '@>' branch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: two branches already implement the same job for different server versions, so a maintainer could copy one branch again.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a json_exists-style builder mirrored in a second datastore module
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Oracle already carries a parallel jsonArrayContains encoder, so a new PostGIS JSON operator would plausibly be mirrored there.

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module build; `mvn -pl modules/plugin/jdbc/jdbc-postgis -am test` (surefire 3.5.3, pom.xml:772)
O10_build.project_tests: PostgisJsonPathExistsTest and PostgisFilterToSQLTest encode filters to SQL with no database (they extend SQLFilterTestSupport, modules/library/jdbc/src/test/java/org/geotools/data/jdbc/SQLFilterTestSupport.java:36); PostGISJsonOnlineTest / PostGISJsonArrayContainsOnlineTest need a live PostGIS server and are not part of the offline path.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Double only the single quotes (value.replace("'", "''")), which does stop the SQL break-out but leaves the JSONPath string unescaped, so the double-quote expectation in the fixed test (fix.diff:43) is still wrong.

out_of_scope_notes: OracleFilterToSQL.jsonExists (modules/plugin/jdbc/jdbc-oracle) implements the same jsonArrayContains SQL generation but already escapes pointer and value (OracleFilterToSQL.java:619-620); outside the advisory's PostGIS scope, not pursued.
